name: Course Shell & Rendering Engine
description: The PHP/JS/CSS infrastructure that serves, renders, navigates, searches, personalizes, and themes the textbook — including the course index, landing page, mobile plumbing, vendor styles, and embed/proxy utilities.

name: Part 1 — Foundations
description: The opening lessons on the history of AI and science, the history of language, and the numerical/linear-algebra/statistical/typo-theory bedrock (math I–IV, statistics I–II, geometry I–III).

name: Part 2 — How Neural Networks Learn
description: The learning mechanics: the smallest network, loss, derivatives and differentiation, backpropagation, automatic differentiation, activation functions, the optimizer, hyperparameters, live training, and reinforcement learning.

name: Part 3 — Deep Learning & Vision
description: Deep learning mechanics (deeplearning lab, ResNets/vanishing gradients, over/underfitting, layer norm, topology of representation) and the computer-vision stack (CNN, deconvolution, Inceptionism, ReLU folding).

name: Part 4 — The Transformer Revolution
description: Tokenization, embeddings, positional encoding, self-attention, the from-scratch trainable transformer with provenance/TDA/layer-summary tooling, and the surrounding theory (diffusion, algorithms, mechanistic interpretability, alternative architectures).

name: Part 5 — Making AI Useful
description: Practical LLM application: prompting, fine-tuning/post-training, RAG and semantic/web search, agents, reasoning, context windows, evaluation, inference/serving, training data and infrastructure, and reliability/safety.

name: Part 6 — Bigger Questions
description: The closing part on the AI ecosystem and frontier: the untold history, the mind, AI beyond LLMs, deep theory, frontier topics, alignment, law, philosophy, unexpected capabilities, AI-for-science, existential risk, myths, software, and the appendix.

name: Standalone Demo Collection (lndw)
description: The standalone interactive presentation decks and supporting demos in lndw/ (the 'Wie funktionieren LLMs' deck, intuition/embedding/attention/philosophy/sheaves slides) and the archived lndw_history/ AI-history deck, plus their bundled vendor libs and precomputed data.

name: Python Reference Implementations
description: Python reference code that mirrors the in-browser lessons: hand-rolled and PyTorch/TF autodiff, minimal-neuron XOR, vision classifiers, plus the QoS AST linter and the Zipf data generator.

name: Formal Verification (Coq)
description: The 19-file Coq formalization of the 'Coherent World Models / Coherent Difference' chapter: the sheaf-theoretic and category-theoretic descent framework, sameness hierarchy, Tarski truth, and its application to LLMs.

name: Test & QA Suite
description: Quality assurance: the tests/ validators (PHP/JS/link/typo/LaTeX/render/lesson-guard, search/topics/keypoint smoke tests, and headless layout-guard fixtures+runners) and the darkmode-ci/ Puppeteer theme-screenshot CI (library, orchestrator, autofix, watch-and-fix).

name: Course Content Docs & Working Notes
description: Top-level prose and working material: README, research/authoring notes and TODOs, image-provenance and dark-mode tracking, research essays, consistency/correction audits, the standalone 'story' explainer, the learnsys adaptive-learning prototypes, and the todo/ drafts (WIP Part 4/6 lessons + formulary).
